title: 2016 AMC8 20
statement: The least common multiple of \(a\) and \(b\) is \(12,\) and the least common multiple of \(b\) and \(c\) is \(15.\) What is the least possible value of the least common multiple of \(a\) and \(c?\)

solutions.text:
We know that \(b\) has to divide both \(12\) and \(15,\) so it must equal either \(1\) or \(3.\)

If \(b = 1,\) then \(a = 12\) and \(c = 15,\) making their least common multiple \(60.\) If \(b = 3,\) then we may take \(a = 4\) and \(c = 5.\) The least common multiple in this scenario is \(20.\)

Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: Since \(b\) appears in both least common multiples, start with possible values of \(b\).
Try to make \(b\) absorb the common factor \(3\) from \(12\) and \(15\).
